name: Occasional One-Sided Getback
definition: For a nonempty binary class $\mathcal H$ on a finite domain $X$, the **Occasional One-Sided Getback** parameter is the minimum, over a permutation $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ of $X$ chosen before play and deterministic prediction rules, of the worst-case number of reported mistakes. At round $t$ the learner predicts $y_t\in\{0,1\}$ using the fixed order and previous feedback. The adversary fixes an unknown target $h\in\mathcal H$ and returns either $*$ (silence) or $1$; a report $1$ is legal only if $y_t\ne h(x_t)$. Silence is allowed on both correct and incorrect predictions and reveals no label. Only reports $1$ are counted. The worst case ranges over targets and legal feedback sequences. For $X=\varnothing$ the value is zero.
graph_summary: Minimum worst-case number of reported mistakes in a learner-chosen fixed domain order, with optional mistake-only feedback.
origin_references: The fixed favorable-order model is background from \cite{ben1997online}. The optional mistake-only variant and signal-counting convention used here are defined in the companion survey; the cited paper is not used as a source for this variant.

monotonic.proof: Any favorable-sequence, one-sided-feedback strategy valid for every target in $\mathcal H$ is still valid after restricting the set of possible targets to a subfamily.
